name: Bennism
summary: Bennism is the democratic socialism associated with Tony Benn and the Labour left from the 1970s: a planned mixed economy with extensive public ownership, industrial democracy, import and capital controls, and the removal of unaccountable power at every level. It paired economic transformation with constitutional radicalism (a republic, an elected second chamber, accountability of rulers) and opposed EEC membership, NATO and nuclear weapons.
scope: The 1974-1981 Alternative Economic Strategy and the broader programme of Tony Benn and his Labour left supporters, including Benn's later constitutional proposals (the Commonwealth of Britain Bill, 1991) and anti-war politics. It excludes the wider socialist movement, and many statements outside British political economy and constitutional questions are unaddressed, so they are low-confidence inferences from his general democratic and anti-racist principles.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Labour left backed a fully state-funded NHS, and Benn's Charter of Rights in the Commonwealth bill lists free healthcare.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Commonwealth bill's charter includes a living wage; Bennites backed a statutory floor under pay as part of redistribution.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Alternative Economic Strategy replaced market allocation with planning, public ownership and import and capital controls.

public-ownership.rationale: Extensive public ownership was a core element of the 1970s programme, including a National Enterprise Board taking stakes in leading firms.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Higher taxation of the rich was an explicit part of Benn's Strategy B.

unions-good.rationale: Benn backed the miners' strike and industrial democracy and defended unions as the base of the Labour movement.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bennism put democratic and social control of industry above property rights; compulsory planning agreements overrode owners' discretion.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Compulsory planning agreements, price controls and control of banks were designed to bring firms under democratic direction.

cut-welfare.rationale: The left of Labour sought to expand the welfare state; the 1983 programme promised higher social spending and reversal of cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: Benn backed the Upper Clyde workers' cooperative and Lucas Aerospace plan, though main emphasis was public ownership plus workers' participation.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Benn's bill demanded annual accountability of security services; a civil-libertarian stance makes broad anti-terror surveillance unwelcome.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Benn's drug policy is not covered in the sources; Labour left opinion on legalisation was mixed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Benn condemned racist rhetoric, but he was also a free-speech civil libertarian; the sources give no view on legal restriction.

strong-leader.rationale: Bennism demanded that leaders answer to members and be removable; Benn denounced concentrated unaccountable power.

state-harmful.rationale: Bennism sought to use the democratised state to plan the economy; it is a statist form of democratic socialism.

limit-guns.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the Labour left's general support for gun control.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not a stated Bennite aim; the bill stressed accountability over military and security services and Benn opposed foreign wars.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not covered by the sources; Labour left opinion was split.

decide-locally.rationale: Bennism backed devolved national parliaments and broad local council freedom but also strong national planning, so it is split.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not directly sourced; inferred from the bill's rights charter and Labour left's generally reformist penal views.

traditional-family.rationale: Not discussed; Benn supported gay liberation and equal rights, which cuts against treating traditional families as the foundation.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Benn supported gay liberation and opposed Section 28 but died before the marriage debate; inferred support.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not covered in the sources; the Labour left generally supported legal abortion, so a low-confidence inference.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Commonwealth bill disestablishes the Church of England and makes the state secular.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Benn backed the Bristol Bus Boycott and condemned Powell, so anti-racism is clear, though affirmative correction is inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; Bennites were split and the sources give no evidence.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Benn framed his republicanism around the Levellers and Chartists rather than national tradition, and was internationalist; inferred.

gradual-change.rationale: The bill proposed sweeping constitutional change, and Benn called the monarchy part of an unfinished democratic revolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Benn condemned Enoch Powell's rhetoric and backed the Bristol Bus Boycott.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Benn wanted Commons approval of UN votes and treaties and rejected unaccountable supranational bodies, but backed the UN over unilateral force.

free-trade.rationale: Strategy B was protectionist: Benn proposed import controls and withdrawal from the EEC.

nation-first.rationale: Bennism's EEC opposition was democratic rather than nationalist, and it was also internationalist; the statement fits only loosely.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Benn led the Stop the War Coalition and opposed the Iraq bombing and Falklands task force; he preferred UN processes.

open-borders.rationale: Not sourced as a position; Benn was anti-racist but did not call for open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: Benn turned against nuclear power but his programme was about reflation and growth through investment.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not sourced for Benn; inferred from his turn against nuclear power and support for public control of energy.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Benn stressed democratic control of science and technology rather than faith in progress alone.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Benn supported nuclear power as a minister but later opposed it on cost, safety and links to weapons.

revolution-justified.rationale: Bennism pursued change through Parliament and constitutional reform, as the Commonwealth bill shows, though Benn warned systems without consent can be overthrown.

experts-over-public.rationale: Benn's five questions demand accountability of every holder of power, and he championed popular democratic control over technocrats.

central-planning.rationale: The AES involved planning agreements and economic planning, though within a mixed economy with import and price controls rather than full central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not explicitly addressed; the AES kept firms under public ownership and workers' participation within a planned mixed economy.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; Benn's tax emphasis was general redistribution.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Higher taxation of the rich was part of Strategy B, and inheritance taxation follows from the programme and abolition of hereditary privilege.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed by sources; Bennites favoured jobs and services over cash transfers.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Import controls were a core element of the Alternative Economic Strategy, which Benn described as withdrawing behind walls to reconstruct.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The National Enterprise Board and compulsory planning agreements were designed to direct investment into leading manufacturing firms.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The programme favoured public and cooperative ownership over dispersed small owners; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bennism was reformist democratic socialism, not a vision of abolishing money; inferred.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Strategy B called for public control of banks and capital movements, not market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Bennism wanted industrial democracy rooted in workers, not state-recognised bodies setting prices with employers; planning agreements were with firms.

one-party-rule.rationale: Benn insisted on democratic accountability and being able to remove rulers; he rejected one-party rule.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Benn's Commonwealth of Britain Bill abolished the monarchy and made the head of state an elected president.

democracy-best.rationale: Benn argued that if you cannot remove those who govern you, you do not live in a democracy, and made democracy central.

direct-votes.rationale: Benn backed referendums on key constitutional questions such as the EEC, but wanted accountable representatives too.

workers-councils.rationale: Benn supported workers' control and workplace democracy but through Parliament, not councils replacing it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Benn backed devolution and Irish unity but opposed Scottish independence.

natural-rulers.rationale: Benn rejected hereditary rule and all unaccountable power as undemocratic.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not directly sourced; Benn was a parliamentary democrat but warned of overthrow without consent.

war-builds-character.rationale: Benn was a leading anti-war voice who opposed the Falklands, Gulf and Iraq wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Commonwealth bill disestablishes the Church of England in a secular Commonwealth.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The bill proposes a democratic secular republic, so laws rest on popular consent, not scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Bennism put public bodies in control of essential functions; privatised security is contrary to it.

military-superiority.rationale: Benn sought withdrawal from NATO and unilateral disarmament and led anti-war campaigns.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Bennism's democratic opposition to the EEC was explicitly non-nationalist, and Benn condemned racism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Benn defended Marxist ideas as an influence on the movement and said power lies with industrialists, bankers and media.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Strategy B sought redistribution through taxation, jobs and public services, though Bennites framed it as democracy and need.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not covered; no evidence of a Bennite position.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not covered; Benn's anti-imperialism suggests sympathy but reparations are unsourced.

civilizational-union.rationale: Bennism opposed supranational blocs on democratic grounds and was internationalist, not civilizational.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Bennism's socialism drew on Christian and radical ethics and sought production for human needs.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The bill enshrines a charter of rights including economic and social ones; inferred against subordinating rights.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Bennism wanted to democratise industry and meet needs through investment, not reject industrialism.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Benn wanted democratic control of science and technology, neither accelerating nor rejecting it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Benn's accountability questions ('how can we get rid of you?') point against rule by algorithms; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Benn wanted security services accountable, but no source addresses encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: Bennism sought democratic transformation, calling the Crown part of an unfinished revolution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Benn rejected pragmatic adjustment as with the 1976 IMF deal and held to a socialist strategy.

direct-action.rationale: Bennism worked chiefly through party and Parliament, though Benn supported strikes and workplace actions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Benn's emphasis on democratic accountability and workers' control suggests means should reflect ends; inferred.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Bennism is an industrial-democracy socialism with no anti-civilizational strand.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of Bennism; it sought industrial democracy within industry.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Benn said public investment should meet human needs, in a socialist tradition of need-based provision.

production-for-use.rationale: Benn argued for public investment to meet 'human needs' as the aim of the economy, replacing corporate capitalism.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Benn defended Marxist analysis as influential and held that capital power over workers needed democratic challenge.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Bennism is a parliamentary democratic socialism that insisted on democratic accountability.

collective-farming.rationale: Not a Bennite policy; inferred against compulsory collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Benn opposed wars as imperialist but sources do not state this causal theory.

taxation-theft.rationale: Higher taxes on the rich were part of Strategy B.

harm-principle.rationale: Benn was a civil libertarian but also supported economic restrictions; not directly addressed.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The bill's charter couples individual rights with collective economic and social rights.

conscription.rationale: Not sourced; anti-militarist stance makes conscription unlikely.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Benn insisted that being able to remove rulers by vote is the test of democracy.

state-as-business.rationale: Bennism wanted democratic public provision for need, not state run on a business model.

positive-liberty.rationale: The charter of rights includes housing, healthcare and a living wage as rights, implying freedom needs material means.

media-academia-power.rationale: Benn said power lay with industrialists, bankers and media, but did not rank them above elected officials.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Benn was a vocal anti-racist who condemned Powell's rhetoric.

organic-representation.rationale: Bennism wanted democratic party and parliamentary accountability, not corporatist representation.

total-state.rationale: Bennism sought democratic accountability and civil liberties, not state direction of culture and education.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not part of Bennism; its aim was democratic socialism.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Anti-imperialist foreign policy and anti-war positions exclude expansionism.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The bill replaces oaths of allegiance to the Crown with an oath to the constitution.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to Bennite radical democracy and abolition of hereditary privilege.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Not addressed by Bennism's sources; the Labour left had no settled epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Benn drew on Christian ethics ('Jesus the prophet') but no source states a view on universal rational moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Bennism assumed class and interest conflict within capitalism and the need for contest over power; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Benn backed Palestinian rights, boycott of Israeli goods and ending arms sales to Israel.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; Benn's Palestine position bears on one case only.

revive-national-language.rationale: Neither Benn's writings nor the sources discuss reviving a lapsed national language, and nothing in Bennite principles settles it.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industrial democracy, with workers participating in strategic company decisions, is a defining Bennite aim.

school-vouchers.rationale: Bennism backed public provision and state planning; vouchers to private schools contradict this.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Reflation was the first element of the AES, rejecting monetarist deficit avoidance.

economic-freedom.rationale: Benn saw capital power as a threat to democracy and proposed capital and import controls.

rule-by-example.rationale: Bennism relies on democratic institutions and accountability, not the moral example of rulers.

national-self-determination.rationale: Benn supported Irish unification and UN-based resolution of disputes; he backed self-determination in anti-imperial contexts.

force-without-un.rationale: Benn argued the Falklands should go to the UN and opposed the Iraq war and Gulf War action.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Benn was a Christian agnostic who combined rationalist and religious ethics.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Benn condemned anti-immigrant rhetoric; inferred opposition to welfare chauvinism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Not directly sourced; Labour left rejected workfare while backing jobs creation.

class-collaboration.rationale: Benn argued that power lay with industrialists and bankers and pushed to shift it to workers, not partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not part of Bennism, which draws on radical English tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: Benn's anti-imperialism points to sympathy with non-aligned cooperation, but no source states this.

workers-nation.rationale: Bennism was internationalist and opposed nationalist framing even of its EEC opposition.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The bill requires gender balance and equal representation for men and women.

ban-interest.rationale: Not part of the programme; Strategy B proposed public control of banks, not banning lending.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Benn backed the Bristol Bus Boycott against a colour bar and condemned Powell.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Benn argued real power lay with industrialists, bankers and media, though he held that the state could be democratised.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not sourced; his opposition to nuclear power came with public energy control, but Benn backed the coal miners and domestic coal.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Benn defended the Bristol Bus Boycott against a colour bar and attacked Powell, so a demand that immigrants abandon their culture is unlikely; the exact view is inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory directly opposed by Benn's condemnation of Powell-style rhetoric.

proportional-representation.rationale: Benn famously opposed PR for Commons but his bill used proportional election for the House of the People.

national-mission.rationale: Bennism's anti-imperialist and anti-war foreign policy rejects missions to spread its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The bill's mandated gender parity reflects recognition of structural disadvantage; not stated as theory.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Benn said that those who govern are unaccountable, but his critique targeted unaccountable power rather than corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is contrary to Benn's equality and human-rights positions.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Benn's bill required security services to justify themselves annually, and he opposed foreign wars.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Bennism demanded extensive public ownership, planning and social rights.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Benn's record of opposing colour bars and racist rhetoric makes discouraging mixed marriage incompatible with his politics.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The bill guarantees fundamental human rights and equal representation for men and women.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Strategy B was a national route to socialism, behind import and capital controls.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not stated; Benn backed Palestinian rights but sources give no general theory.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Religious personal law is not covered in the sources; secular equal citizenship fits Bennism but so does minority-rights caution.

restrict-conversion.rationale: A secular constitution with a charter of fundamental rights, as in the Commonwealth bill, leaves no basis for restricting conversion.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A secular Commonwealth would not legislate religious dietary taboos; the position is inferred from the bill's secularism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The bill is secular but Benn was Methodist-influenced; no source on schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Bennism is democratic and opposed to authoritarian state strengthening.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Benn argued that no system can long survive without a high and continuing degree of consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Import controls aimed at employment, not an export-surplus goal; not directly stated.

population-transfer.rationale: Pressuring a minority to leave contradicts Benn's anti-racist record and the bill's rights charter.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Benn opposed foreign wars, but his programme embraced coercive taxation and compulsory planning, so he would not hold the libertarian formulation.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Bennism rejects competitive capitalism in favour of planned cooperation and need.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Benn was a civil libertarian who urged Sinn Fein to take Westminster seats; inferred against banning.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Benn's questions about power and removing rulers parallel the non-domination idea; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: Benn wanted all power accountable and Parliament supreme, but proposed a federal structure; no direct view.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bennism stressed membership accountability and democratic party control, not vanguardism.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Redistribution, jobs and public services priorities for working people were central to Bennite programmes.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: The Labour left opposed Thatcher's council house sales and promoted public housing; the 1983 manifesto is a source for this orientation.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Benn backed the miners' strike and defended trade union rights against legal restriction throughout his career.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Bennism saw poverty as caused by economic institutions and power.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Benn campaigned against racism and condemned Powell, rejecting the claim that diversity undermines society.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Benn wanted elected accountable officials; sortition is not part of the bill.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Benn's bill entrenches a charter of rights and accountability of the security services.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price controls formed part of the Alternative Economic Strategy; fixing food prices in scarcity fits that approach, though food specifically is inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Bennism stressed democratic accountability and free expression; not control by a ruling party.

party-commands-army.rationale: The bill has forces swear allegiance to the constitution and Commons approval of foreign policy.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Not sourced; Benn's anti-racist record suggests opposition to making citizenship harder to obtain.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Benn's accountability ethos fits it and he gave up the peerage, but pay rules are unsourced.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Bennites wanted leaders accountable to members but Benn also defied party leadership.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Bennism opposed EU membership on democratic grounds because the Commission cannot be removed.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The bill makes a ceremonial president and puts powers with Parliament.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Disestablishment would let the church choose its own hierarchy, so no stake in bishops.

clerical-rule.rationale: The Commonwealth bill is a democratic secular republic that disestablishes the church, so rule by senior clerics is excluded.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Benn opposed wars but acted through Parliament and the anti-war movement, not by seeking national defeat.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Benn was a civil libertarian, and nothing in Bennism supports state censorship on moral grounds; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The bill limits the president to a fixed term of up to six years.

recall-officials.rationale: Benn's fifth question was 'How can we get rid of you?'; accountability by removal is central.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Benn sought withdrawal from NATO, and his bill made stationing foreign forces unconstitutional.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Bennite and Labour-left housing policy centred on expanding council rented housing, not abolishing renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Replacing the army with an armed citizenry is not part of Bennite policy; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Bennism arose from the industrial labour movement and has no agrarian moral thesis; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Benn supported Irish unification and the bill ended Northern Ireland's separate jurisdiction.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Benn blamed concentrated industrial, financial and media power, not graduates; mild inference.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred from Benn's anti-racism and anti-imperialism, since no source states a theory of cultures.

death-penalty.rationale: Benn opposed capital punishment as a Labour left MP; inferred from Labour left consensus.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the bill's gender equality and Benn's support for gay rights.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The bill's secular republic and Benn's disestablishment stance point against teaching creationism in state schools; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Benn's civil libertarianism and Labour-left feminist concern pull in opposite directions; no source records his view.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Descent-based citizenship is inconsistent with Benn's anti-racist stance and the Commonwealth bill's equal-rights approach.

minority-language-support.rationale: The bill creates national parliaments for Scotland and Wales; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Sources say nothing about exemptions from general law; secular equality and minority protection point in different directions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nothing in the sources on cultural conformity; Benn was a civil libertarian but this is not a Bennite theme.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not sourced; inferred from anti-imperialist and anti-IMF positions after 1976.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Not directly addressed; inferred from Benn's view that economic power must be democratised.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The bill proposes a written constitution, though through Parliament and referendum.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Benn's whole programme rests on democratic accountability, so suspending freedoms for development is excluded.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not sourced; inferred from Benn's internationalism and anti-imperialist politics.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The 1983 programme called for unilateral nuclear disarmament, which Bennites backed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The bill has parliament elect the president by two-thirds, not direct election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Strategy B called for control of banks, capital and economic planning under democratic government.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The sources do not touch on this; Benn backed Palestinian rights and Irish unification by consent, leaving the general rule unclear.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Compulsory planning agreements and public ownership subordinate property to common needs.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Not sourced; Benn criticised Soviet-style socialism but no source gives this term.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from Benn's turn against nuclear power on safety grounds.

collective-defense.rationale: Benn sought withdrawal from NATO, whose core is collective defence, and wanted its membership subject to democratic review.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Sources do not address annexation; Benn's anti-imperialism suggests sympathy but he made no general statement here.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The bill disestablishes the church, but curbing its property is unsourced.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The bill has an elected ceremonial president, a symbolic role; sources do not discuss this.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Benn opposed Scottish independence but backed Irish self-determination; sources do not say force.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The bill's federal design gives nations wide autonomy but sources say nothing of regions joining a larger state with a separate economic system.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The bill abolishes the monarchy and every royal title, and Benn argued the Crown is an undemocratic symbol.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Strategy B called for higher taxation of the rich, which a flat rate would contradict.

character-from-environment.rationale: Bennism located inequality in economic and political institutions rather than innate nature; this is an inference about upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Contrary to the bill's constitutionalism and 'all power accountable'.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; Bennism's emphasis on meeting human needs at home suggests space is not a central goal.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The bill abolishes the monarchy and Lords for democratic election.

leader-cult.rationale: Contrary to republicanism and Benn's critique of unaccountable power.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no Bennite position on custody rules is documented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Not sourced; Bennism sought democratic accountability within institutions.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; Commonwealth bill nationalised Crown estates but no land redistribution.

refugee-return.rationale: Benn backed Palestinian rights, so right of return for refugees is a likely inference, but no source states it.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Territorial claims based on nationality contradict Bennism's non-nationalist, internationalist and anti-imperialist stance.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The bill's charter of rights and secular state exclude punishing religious departure.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compelling dress is inconsistent with the equal-rights and secular provisions of the Commonwealth bill.

common-currency.rationale: Benn opposed EEC and EU integration, and monetary union would constrain democratic economic control.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Bennism's opposition to supranational union rested on democratic accountability and it was internationalist, not ethno-linguistic.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Not addressed; Benn's devolution proposals were territorial, not cultural-personal autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The sources give no view on diaspora strategy; the statement has no Bennite counterpart.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Benn defended Marxist ideas as an influence but did not adopt a strict materialism.

ban-cartels.rationale: Bennism sought public ownership and planning, not competition policy.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bennite policy was public ownership of failing firms rather than bailout without control.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Benn put democratic parliament supreme but the bill also entrenches rights.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The bill requires a gender-balanced House of the People and paired MPs.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Strategy B was protectionist but meant to rebuild industry, not close a colonial bloc to all trade; Benn called both extremes a siege economy.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Bennism preferred import controls to trade agreements, and sources give no view on standards clauses.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not addressed; Bennism emphasised industrial democracy, not replacing material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Bennism pursued a parliamentary road to socialism and rejected insurrectionary strategy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Benn renounced his peerage and the bill ends titles and the honours system.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Not addressed; Benn's radical-tradition appeals were domestic.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Contrary to the anti-imperialist foreign policy that Benn maintained from Suez to Iraq.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred; oath-of-allegiance reform suggests low interest in loyalty rituals.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not directly sourced; Benn's anti-racism leans against abolishing such measures.

public-money-creation.rationale: Strategy B proposed public control of banks and insurance, which supports public money creation; the exact monetary mechanism is not stated.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bennism argued reform within corporate capitalism had failed and sought a transition.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Bennism's anti-imperialism excludes projecting influence over former imperial territories.

delink-world-market.rationale: Strategy B was national, but the statement concerns poor countries; not addressed.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Benn pressed workers' solidarity and defended their interests within Britain, not a theory that they share imperial profits.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Benn backed the boycott of a bus company's colour bar, so he opposed private freedom to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The bill proposes a written constitution with a charter of rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; Benn's anti-imperialism suggests sympathy but he left no stated position.

elective-rulers.rationale: The bill has an elected president and an elected second chamber in place of the monarchy and Lords.

minority-veto.rationale: Bennism is majoritarian democratic socialism and would not let one dissenter block collective decisions.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Benn said without consent systems are overthrown, but sources don't state a right to resist.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Benn transferred prerogative powers to Parliament but also entrenched constitution.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The sources do not cover animal welfare in Benn's politics.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The sources do not cover animal use in Benn's politics.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Benn rejected hierarchy and paternalism, favouring democratic power.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Bennism is built on mass participation, as in the five questions on power and the push for accountable party members.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Benn criticised media power over politics but sources do not link mass culture to social reproduction.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Benn said power rests with industrialists, bankers and media but did not state a theory of cultural hegemony.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, which concern British domestic strategy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Barring naturalised citizens from office contradicts Benn's anti-racist record.

party-own-road.rationale: Strategy B was a national road to socialism; support for each party's own road is inferred.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Not addressed; Benn's national strategy is not a theory of development aid.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Revanchist territorial demands conflict with Benn's internationalist and anti-war stance.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Benn's democratic equal-rights outlook leans against rule by descent group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from Benn's life-long anti-racism; no source mentions constitutional value-setting.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Benn opposed Soviet-style authoritarianism but rejected Cold War framing; sources do not state a view on equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Revisionism that downplays slavery conflicts with Benn's radical democratic and anti-racist tradition.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Not sourced; the bill ends titles and royal honours, suggesting little attachment to commemorating contested figures.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The bill claims democratic universality, so civilization-specific political forms are unlikely to be endorsed; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The bill has forces swear allegiance to the constitution and puts foreign policy under Commons approval, excluding political guardianship.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the bill's social rights charter including free childcare and a living wage.

office-by-exam.rationale: Bennites sought elected and accountable officials; examination-based appointment contradicts that, though not discussed directly.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Strategy B's capital and import controls plus planning of leading firms.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not sourced; inferred from Benn's support for personal and equal rights.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Mandatory reselection of MPs and Benn's accountability questions bring representatives under their members' control, though no source states binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private pension accounts cut against Bennite public provision and the Labour left's defence of the state pension.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Benn's bill nationalised the Crown estates but sources do not support use-based community tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Benn insisted that all power be accountable and transferred prerogative powers to Parliament; inferred for budgets.

single-official-language.rationale: The bill gave Wales and Scotland their own parliaments, which sits badly with one compulsory language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Strategy B controlled capital flows but sources do not mention land purchases by foreigners.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Not addressed; anti-racism points toward sympathy but the legal doctrine is not discussed.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not addressed; Bennism criticised corporate power but not consumer culture.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Benn opposed foreign interventions from the Falklands to Iraq, so covert arming of insurgents contradicts his stance.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Intervention to hold an ally in a bloc contradicts Bennite anti-imperialism and rejection of alliances.

corporate-influence.rationale: Benn argued power rested with industrialists, bankers and media.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Strategy B controlled capital flows, but sources do not address NGO or university funding.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed; housing localism and anti-second-home sentiment exist on the left but no Bennite source says so.

job-guarantee.rationale: AES prioritised saving jobs and reflation for full employment.

democratic-peace.rationale: Benn opposed Western wars waged in democracy's name, but sources give no view on the empirical thesis.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Benn campaigned through Parliament and said consent underpins legitimacy, suggesting a general duty to obey; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Benn opposed interventions but backed Palestine, so not absolute.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial democracy implies unity of all workers in a firm; inferred, not stated.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Benn campaigned against racism, rejecting minority-conspiracy theories.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; the bill's charter seeks equal rights but no source questions marriage law.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Benn's bill required security services to justify themselves annually and put foreign policy under Commons control.

local-production.rationale: Not addressed; Strategy B was national import control rather than localism.

informal-organisation.rationale: Bennism worked through Labour Party, unions and Parliament and campaigned for party democracy.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Benn put Parliament above the EEC but also wanted Commons approval of UN treaties; the general question is not addressed.

religious-nation.rationale: The bill creates a secular Commonwealth and disestablishes the Church of England.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tribute to a hegemon is contrary to the anti-imperialist and sovereignty-focused foreign policy of Bennism.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: National parliaments would control most things, but sources do not say they would keep local revenue; planning and redistribution lean against it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Inferred: democratic socialism in the Labour tradition targets industry and finance, not personal belongings.

defeat-communism.rationale: Benn sought withdrawal from NATO and opposed Cold War alliances, so aggressive anti-communism is outside his view.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Benn and the Labour left favoured fully public provision and renationalisation, not a mixed market of providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Benn called himself a Christian agnostic and drew on Jesus as a prophet, which leans against the statement, but that is his personal faith, not a Bennite position.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Benn defended Marxist ideas but sources give no judgement on capitalism's historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the bill's economic and social rights charter alongside gender parity.

socialized-care.rationale: The bill lists free childcare as a right, but sources do not address housework.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Linguistic purism has no place in Bennism's internationalist outlook; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Bennism relied on national planning and public ownership rather than small property-holding communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: State-encouraged settlement to alter regional demographics contradicts Benn's anti-racist politics.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Benn rejected corporate capitalism and also criticised Soviet-style rule, but did not present his programme as a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Benn backed Palestinian rights, which leans against historical claims taking precedence; inferred.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Benn's long anti-racist record excludes Holocaust denial; inferred.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Benn supported gay liberation, opposed Section 28 and backed equalising the age of consent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Benn argued that democracy requires being able to remove rulers, so suppression of opposition is excluded.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: A secular Commonwealth with a rights charter has no blasphemy laws.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Contrary to the anti-imperialist foreign policy of Bennism.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty in Islamic law is outside the sources; Benn opposed invasions of Muslim countries.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Bennism holds that legitimacy comes from democratic consent, not religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Industrial democracy and accountability to members were core, and Benn urged ordinary people to hold power to account.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Benn opposed class, race and sex oppression but sources do not show him arguing they must be addressed together.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Benn died before the debate matured and sources are silent.

assisted-dying.rationale: The sources do not record Benn's view on assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Bennism is an openly socialist left project and rejected centrist blending.

alienated-labor.rationale: Benn defended Marxist ideas as an influence on Labour; alienation is not a documented Bennite theme.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Benn rejected racist and anti-minority claims and opposed wars against Muslim countries.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Benn grounded legitimacy in popular consent and democratic accountability, not in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The bill is secular but sources do not address dress codes.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not sourced; inferred from pro-worker, pro-equality positions.

social-market-economy.rationale: Bennism sought a socialist alternative rather than a regulated market economy, and was against corporate capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Unilateral nuclear disarmament and NATO withdrawal did not extend to abolishing all armed forces in the sources.

rich-first.rationale: Strategy B's redistribution and planning contradict letting some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Benn sought NATO withdrawal, and the bill made NATO membership subject to democratic review.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The bill ends the hereditary monarchy and all titles, replacing them with elected office.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Strategy B favoured public control of banks, but mutual credit banks are not mentioned.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The AES was proposed as an alternative to the IMF loan that the Cabinet accepted in December 1976; Benn opposed it.

property-franchise.rationale: Benn argued all political power should be democratically elected, and the bill lowers the voting age to 16.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist theory is not part of the documented Bennite programme.

reification.rationale: The Marxist concept is not addressed in the sources.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Benn argued that power lies with industrialists, bankers and the media, not with voters.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Benn favoured a written constitution and accountable power, but case-by-case decrees are not addressed.

racial-franchise.rationale: Racial limits on voting conflict with Benn's anti-racism and democratic principle.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the bill's accountability provisions for security services and foreign policy.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: A charter of rights in a secular state excludes restricting marriage by religion.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Benn supported the Bristol Bus Boycott against a colour bar, opposing discrimination.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The bill favours elected bodies and referendums; randomly selected assemblies are not mentioned.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Benn's own faith was Christian-socialist and reform-minded, but no source addresses interpretation of religious law.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Benn argued that power rested with industrialists and bankers rather than voters and sought to subject wealth to democratic control.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from Benn's support for gay liberation and equal rights.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Benn was a Christian agnostic and his bill separates church and state without promoting atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not part of Bennism, which sought democratic accountability of the state security apparatus rather than abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The sources do not address consociational power-sharing; Benn's Irish unification by consent is the nearest, unrelated, position.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Bennism and the 1983 programme relied on public welfare, not charity.

term-limits.rationale: The bill fixed four-year terms and a limit for the president, but sources do not address terms for all offices.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy is not in the sources; Benn favoured accountable representatives and referendums.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Unilateral nuclear disarmament relates to extinction risk but no source frames it as a top priority generally.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from Benn's equal-rights stance; sources do not mention it.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The bill guarantees equal rights for men and women, so shared marital authority follows by inference.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from Benn's anti-racism and democratic inclusion; sources do not state this.

rent-control.rationale: Public housing and tenant protections were Labour-left policy; rent caps are inferred from price controls.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Drilled national-service youth movements contradict Bennite anti-militarism and civil libertarianism; inferred.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Benn's bill barred foreign forces and he backed unilateral nuclear disarmament, implying no US weapons based in Britain.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The Commonwealth bill makes stationing foreign forces on its soil unconstitutional.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Higher taxes on the rich and public ownership aimed to shift rewards from capital to labour.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Benn was a strong anti-war voice but not a documented absolute pacifist.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Benn grounded his politics in a radical tradition of Levellers and Chartists rather than ancient national origins; inferred.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Benn was anti-militarist, and the bill ends honours and titles; martyr cults for the nation are inconsistent.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Benn drew on Christian socialism but framed politics as democratic accountability, not cosmic struggle.

culture-before-state.rationale: Bennism was oriented towards political and economic change, not cultural renewal first.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: An ethnic economic preference contradicts Benn's anti-racist stance.

independent-unions.rationale: Benn backed the miners' strike and unions as independent actors in industrial democracy; independence from a Labour government is inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Industrial democracy and Benn's question of whether those in power are accountable make workers' power the test of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Extensive public ownership and meeting human needs are core Bennite aims, which extends to water, hospitals and transport.

second-chamber.rationale: Bill replaces Lords with elected House of the People so bicameral retained.

municipal-property.rationale: Bennism favoured national public ownership and planning rather than municipal-only ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The bill proposes federal national parliaments, not municipal confederalism.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; the bill's living-wage right is not framed around family support.

person-over-state.rationale: The charter of rights and accountability of the state imply individuals are not mere means, though Bennism is collectivist.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Benn's Christian-socialist views suggest sympathy, but no source states it as a political principle.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The bill's federal structure gives national parliaments constitutional powers rather than revocable ones.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Benn's politics were class-based and anti-racist, not organised around racial group interests.

racial-pride.rationale: Benn's emphasis on class and anti-racism lean against racial pride politics; not addressed directly.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Benn opposed the Falklands, Gulf and Iraq wars and sought withdrawal from military alliances.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Bennism's opposition to blocs was not nationalist and it supported British federation; inferred.

communal-electorates.rationale: Religiously separate electorates contradict a secular unitary electoral approach such as the bill's.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Not documented; Bennism's concerns were about capital and unaccountable power, not foreign partition plots.

free-public-college.rationale: Not sourced; Benn's charter of social rights and Labour-left backing of public provision suggest support for tuition-free public higher education.

capital-controls.rationale: Strategy B included capital and export controls alongside control of banks and insurers.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not sourced for Benn; inferred from his turn against nuclear power and support for public control of energy, though he favoured public ownership over market taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Not directly sourced; inferred from Benn's opposition to nuclear power and weapons as dangers passed to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not address this; Benn backed equality but there is no documented view on distinct values, so it is a split-or-silent case.

arms-reduction.rationale: The 1983 Labour programme and Benn's anti-war politics call for unilateral nuclear disarmament and opposed NATO and foreign forces on British soil.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The Commonwealth of Britain Bill puts treaties under Commons approval and Benn demanded accountability of the security services and foreign policy.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: Benn backed accountable democratic state institutions, though he opposed militarism and nuclear arms; no source discusses armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: Benn was a leading anti-war voice, but he worked through Parliament and stressed legal accountability rather than urging soldiers to disobey.

collective-bargaining.rationale: The Labour left was tied to the trade unions and its programme and Arguments for Socialism defended union bargaining and industrial democracy.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred: the Labour left favoured higher wages, public ownership and welfare over tax-credit top-ups, which were a later development.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The Alternative Economic Strategy aimed at expansionary public spending and planning, and Benn opposed external constraints on government economic control.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: Benn opposed the EEC and backed import controls and anti-imperial politics, but his programme was mainly national in focus.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Benn sought to democratise the state through Parliament, a republic and an elected second chamber, not to destroy it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred: the Alternative Economic Strategy was a planned national programme, though industrial democracy and cooperatives allowed local variety.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: the Labour left stressed public ownership and planning, not valuing ecosystems as capital; Benn's later environmental concern is not documented in the sources.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: Benn stressed democratic sovereignty and opposed the EEC, but his politics were internationalist and secular rather than a sacred view of the nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred: Benn backed free education and opposed fees; cancelling student debt is a modern issue consistent with that.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: Benn backed regional development and devolution within a democratic Britain, but sources do not discuss the colonial analogy.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred: the Charter of Rights in the Commonwealth bill grounds rights in common humanity, but nothing is said on redesigning human nature.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: Benn criticised press concentration and defended the BBC as public, though he also attacked its bias.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Benn was a Christian with strong respect for other faiths, but the sources record no view on whether religions share one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: The Alternative Economic Strategy sought a planned mixed economy with state direction of key sectors, which fits state support for farmers, though Benn opposed the EEC's farm policy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Bennism opposed nuclear weapons and NATO and the Labour left backed unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: Benn worked to make Labour the party of working people and its democratisation was central, though within Labour rather than as a separate party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his anti-racist and human-rights principles and the Charter of Rights in the Commonwealth bill.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his support for equal rights and the Charter of Rights in his Commonwealth bill.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and nothing in Bennite principles bears on it.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: the Bennite programme relied on public planning and state control, not on private lawsuits in place of agencies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Benn proposed an elected second chamber and removal of unelected power, so formal seats for traditional leaders contradict that.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Bennites backed planning and public control but also stressed liberty and accountability.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from his civil-liberties and anti-authoritarian stance, which favours judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from his anti-racist principles and opposition to coercive integration, though encouragement was likely welcome.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Benn was a lifelong champion of trade unions and workers' control, so he would oppose rules that weaken union membership.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his civil-liberties and anti-establishment stance, which would see ID requirements as a barrier to voting.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Benn's Commonwealth of Britain Bill disestablished the Church of England, ending any privileged religious position in the state.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Benn held that democracy means real accountability of power at every level, not only periodic elections, so procedure alone is not enough.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his socially liberal record on gay rights and equality.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his proposed charter of rights and demand for accountable security services.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his support for universal public provision and public ownership over replacing welfare with cash transfers.

women-suffrage.rationale: Equal political rights follow directly from his democratic principles and Commonwealth Bill's equal citizenship.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; Benn was personally sympathetic to religion and socialist analysis locates oppression in class power, so inferred disagreement.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from his anti-racist record.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Labour-left support for state equality machinery and his equality principles.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Bennism holds that property serves the common good and favours public ownership, so a natural right of first claim is rejected.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Benn opposed the Iraq war and held rulers answerable for war; support for international trial of aggression is inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Benn drew on Christian socialism but not on literalism, and the sources do not discuss scripture; inferred as disfavoured.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Benn's democratic and anti-racist principles are inferred to support gender equality in self-government.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The Alternative Economic Strategy favoured planning, but Benn was a democratic socialist critical of bureaucracy; adherents are inferred to be split.

indirect-election.rationale: The Commonwealth bill and Benn's insistence on elective rulers favour direct popular election.

national-church-status.rationale: The Commonwealth of Britain Bill disestablishes the Church of England, so special legal status is rejected.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The Commonwealth bill devolves power to nations and regions; territorial autonomy for minority-majority regions is inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: The audit records support for national self-determination, from which a vote by inhabitants is inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Benn opposed imperialism, but the sources do not address post-colonial borders; inferred as split.

simple-living.rationale: Sources do not discuss a limited-needs ethic for Bennism; inferred as split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Benn's internationalist and anti-racist principles are inferred to oppose restricting settlement.

equal-conscription.rationale: The audit records opposition to conscription, so applying it to neither sex is the closer fit; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Bennism is internationalist and anti-nationalist in tone and the sources never discuss ancestral land; inferred from its general principles, so no clear position.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Benn's Charter of Rights and accountability agenda stress due process and limits on state power, and he was a lifelong civil libertarian, so killing without trial is rejected.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred: Bennites opposed alignment with NATO and the US but the sources say nothing on China, so a mild disagreement with the framing is all that can be inferred.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from Benn's internationalism: the sources do not address kin minorities abroad, and the idea of an ethnic nation is not a Bennite theme.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Bennites favoured public ownership of key resources and investment, which fits common ownership, but the compensation framing is a Georgist idea the sources never mention.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Benn's civil-liberties charter of rights that persons hold rights over their own bodies, but the sources do not discuss self-ownership as a principle, and Bennites reject its libertarian use over labour.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: the Alternative Economic Strategy preferred taxing wealth and the rich over regressive taxes, so cutting consumption taxes fits, but the sources do not mention them directly.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Benn's Labour left backed universal, state-provided services such as the NHS, and opposed means-testing as divisive.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Benn held that parties, unions and citizens should hold rulers to account and rejected personal leadership of a nation, so bypassing parties for a leader is opposed.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Benn's programme aimed at removing unaccountable economic and political power, including that of big business and the City, which implies opposing privileges for connected firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred: Benn was secularist and supported disestablishing the church in the Commonwealth bill, but did not address denominational politics such as in Northern Ireland directly.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The sources never address this synthesis, and Benn's attitude to technology (anti-nuclear, pro-planning) does not suggest a view on ancestral values.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Benn's feminism and rights charter, since the sources do not address divorce law.

national-resource-control.rationale: The Alternative Economic Strategy sought national control of investment, capital and industry and Bennites opposed EEC rules on it.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Strategy B included higher taxation of the rich and capital controls, implying that unequal outcomes can be corrected whatever their origin.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred: Strategy B's capital and exchange controls (s4) fit curbing speculation, but no such tax is cited.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: Benn took anti-racist stands (s5) and would not say racism had ceased to be a main obstacle; not discussed directly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from Benn's stress on accountability and consent of the governed (s2), but his view of unjust law is not documented there.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred: Benn backed planning and democratic control of technology and investment (s6); automation to cut work is not directly addressed.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from opposition to the EEC and NATO and a foreign policy independent of blocs (s1, s3), not from a stated multipolar theory.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred: socialist arguments for workers' control (s6) rest on labour creating wealth, but Benn is not documented stating a labour theory of value.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: Benn's EEC opposition rested on national self-government for working people (s1, s6), though he also stressed internationalism.

material-over-identity.rationale: Split: Benn put economic transformation first but also backed anti-racism and gay rights (s5), so he did not rank identity issues lower.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred: Bennism is democratic socialism built on accountability and elected rulers (s2), so it opposes one-party communist rule.

missingStatements.text: Powers exercised in the monarch's name, such as making treaties and declaring war, should be transferred to the elected parliament.
missingStatements.rationale: The Commonwealth of Britain Bill transfers Royal Prerogative powers to Parliament and puts treaties and UN votes under Commons approval.

missingStatements.text: The state should control the movement of capital in and out of the country.
missingStatements.rationale: Strategy B included capital and export controls alongside control of banks and insurers.

notes: Bennism is a programme more than a doctrine; most social-policy answers are inferences from Benn's personal record. Benn opposed proportional representation for the Commons, yet his bill used it for an elected second chamber.
